name: Codex Review & Notify Code Owner

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
    branches:
      - main
      - develop
      - epic

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

jobs:
  review-and-notify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install requests

      - name: Run Codex Review & Notify
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          CODEX_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CODEX_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          python - << 'EOF'
          import os
          import json
          import requests
          import re

          # Configuration
          GITHUB_TOKEN = os.getenv("GITHUB_TOKEN")
          CODEX_API_KEY = os.getenv("CODEX_API_KEY")
          REPO = "Asymmetric-al/core"
          
          # Get PR details from GitHub context
          pr_number = os.getenv("GITHUB_REF_NAME") # This might not be the PR number directly in all contexts
          # Better way to get PR number in a PR trigger
          pr_number = os.getenv("GITHUB_REF").split("/")[-1] if "refs/pull/" in os.getenv("GITHUB_REF") else None
          
          if not pr_number:
              # Fallback for testing or if env var is structured differently
              # In GitHub Actions, for PR events, we can often derive it or use the event path
              import sys
              if os.path.exists("/github/event.json"):
                  with open("/github/event.json") as f:
                      event = json.load(f)
                      pr_number = event.get("pull_request", {}).get("number")
              else:
                  print("Could not determine PR number. Exiting.")
                  sys.exit(0)

          print(f"Processing PR #{pr_number}")

          # 1. Fetch PR details
          headers = {
              "Authorization": f"token {GITHUB_TOKEN}",
              "Accept": "application/vnd.github.v3+json"
          }
          
          pr_url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{REPO}/pulls/{pr_number}"
          pr_response = requests.get(pr_url, headers=headers)
          
          if pr_response.status_code != 200:
              print(f"Failed to fetch PR: {pr_response.text}")
              exit(1)
              
          pr_data = pr_response.json()
          title = pr_data.get("title", "")
          body = pr_data.get("body", "")
          files_url = pr_data.get("url") + "/files"
          
          # 2. Fetch changed files
          files_response = requests.get(files_url, headers=headers)
          if files_response.status_code != 200:
              print(f"Failed to fetch files: {files_response.text}")
              exit(1)
              
          changed_files = files_response.json()
          file_paths = [f["filename"] for f in changed_files]
          
          # 3. Determine Code Owners
          # Simple heuristic: check CODEOWNERS file if it exists, otherwise default to repo admins or specific team
          # For this example, we'll assume a simple mapping or fetch CODEOWNERS
          codeowners_url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{REPO}/contents/CODEOWNERS"
          codeowners_response = requests.get(codeowners_url, headers=headers)
          
          code_owners = []
          if codeowners_response.status_code == 200:
              import base64
              content = base64.b64decode(codeowners_response.json()["content"]).decode("utf-8")
              # Simple parsing of CODEOWNERS
              for line in content.split("\n"):
                  if line.startswith("#") or not line.strip():
                      continue
                  parts = line.split()
                  if len(parts) >= 2:
                      pattern = parts[0]
                      owners = parts[1:]
                      # Check if any changed file matches the pattern
                      for fp in file_paths:
                          if fnmatch.fnmatch(fp, pattern):
                              code_owners.extend(owners)
          else:
              # Default fallback if no CODEOWNERS or error
              code_owners = ["@Asymmetric-al/core-team"]

          # Remove duplicates
          code_owners = list(set(code_owners))
          
          if not code_owners:
              code_owners = ["@Asymmetric-al/core-team"]

          # 4. Call Codex API (Mocked/Placeholder for actual Codex integration)
          # Since "Codex" isn't a standard public API with a fixed endpoint in this context,
          # we will simulate the review process or use a placeholder if a specific endpoint was intended.
          # Assuming a hypothetical Codex API endpoint for code review.
          
          review_comment = ""
          try:
              # Hypothetical Codex API call
              # codex_url = "https://api.codex.ai/v1/review"
              # payload = {
              #     "repo": REPO,
              #     "pr_number": pr_number,
              #     "files": file_paths,
              #     "title": title,
              #     "body": body
              # }
              # codex_response = requests.post(codex_url, json=payload, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {CODEX_API_KEY}"})
              # if codex_response.status_code == 200:
              #     review_comment = codex_response.json().get("comment", "Review complete.")
              
              # For the purpose of this workflow, we generate a summary based on the PR body and files
              review_comment = f"## Codex Review Summary\n\n"
              review_comment += f"- **PR Title**: {title}\n"
              review_comment += f"- **Files Changed**: {len(file_paths)}\n"
              review_comment += f"- **Code Owners**: {', '.join(code_owners)}\n\n"
              
              # Check for specific keywords in PR body to add context
              if "Next.js" in body or "next" in title.lower():
                  review_comment += "- **Note**: Next.js changes detected. Ensure compatibility checks are passed.\n"
              if "test" in title.lower() or "test" in body.lower():
                  review_comment += "- **Note**: Test changes detected. Verify coverage impact.\n"
                  
          except Exception as e:
              review_comment = f"Error during Codex review: {str(e)}"

          # 5. Post Comment to PR
          comment_url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{REPO}/issues/{pr_number}/comments"
          comment_payload = {
              "body": review_comment
          }
          
          comment_response = requests.post(comment_url, json=comment_payload, headers=headers)
